thread:
maya (product): quick idea — can we make tier routing + fallback configuration editable as a single policy object in the console? keeps free/pro/enterprise rules in one place instead of 3 pages
liam (eng-platform): yes, makes sense. main concern: validation and how we expose soft vs hard quota behavior in the UI
sofia (eng-runtime): runtime needs an explicit, machine-readable field for fallback precedence and backoff behavior. otherwise the router ends up doing heuristics that are hard to reproduce
noah (devex): UX question: should the console show a simulated decision path? e.g., tenant X in eu-west with 90% usage -> show which model variant and fallback would be chosen and why
maya (product): exactly — a "decisions" panel would be helpful for audits + support. also show token-count effect and estimated latency change :chart_with_upwards_trend:
liam (eng-platform): rough sketch of the policy DSL I had in mind:
```yaml
policy_name: tiered-routing-2026-03
tiers:
  free:
    primary: model-small-v1
    fallback:
      - model-small-quantized-v1
      - model-micro-latency-v1
    quota:
      soft_limit_tokens_per_min: 10000
      hard_limit_tokens_per_min: 12000
      soft_behavior: degrade_priority
  pro:
    primary: model-medium-v2
    fallback:
      - model-medium-quantized-v2
    quota:
      soft_limit_tokens_per_min: 200000
      hard_limit_tokens_per_min: 250000
      soft_behavior: burst_with_throttle
  enterprise:
    primary: model-large-v1
    fallback: []
    quota:
      soft_limit_tokens_per_min: 2000000
      hard_limit_tokens_per_min: 2500000
      soft_behavior: no_degrade
routing_overrides:
  regions:
    eu-west:
      prefer_low_latency: true
      fallback_order: [model-medium-latency-v2, model-medium-quantized-v2]
rollout:
  canary: 5%  # route 5% of traffic to new policy
  start_time: 2026-03-19T08:00:00Z
```
sofia (eng-runtime): that looks workable. we need explicit telemetry hooks: emit "policy_decision" events with these fields: tenant, tier, region, chosen_variant, reason, token_count, latency_estimate
liam (eng-platform): +1 telemetry. also add a flag for "policy_strictness" (lenient|strict) so console can toggle whether hard limits are enforced or just logged for a period
noah (devex): can we wire an "explain" button that runs the policy engine against a synthetic request and returns the decision trace? short one-liner trace in the UI, expanded JSON for SREs
maya (product): requirements for the console copy: 1) show active policy version, 2) show effective per-tenant overrides, 3) allow quick rollback to previous policy, 4) surface quota burn rate and projected exhaustion time
liam (eng-platform): implementation notes: store policies in config-service as versioned blobs. router downloads latest policy bundle + delta replay. canary handled by weighted routing in control-plane
sofia (eng-runtime): runtime edgecases: when a fallback variant has incompatible kv-cache shape we must skip it and pick the next. add "compatibility_checks" in the policy metadata
maya (product): question for sales: should enterprise be allowed to opt into "aggressive_fallbacks"? that reduces cost but may alter output quality
liam (eng-platform): flag it as an enterprise opt-in in the policy. UI will show quality/cost tradeoff with examples
ops-bot: deploy-bot: policy service canary roll started for policy tiered-routing-2026-03 at 2026-03-19T08:00:00Z (5% traffic) :rocket:
noah (devex): follow-ups: 1) mockups for the decisions panel by EOD Friday 2) sample policy editor with validation errors inline 3) add unit tests for precedence order
maya (product): tiny UX/scenario: free tier hitting soft quota should be shown as "reduced throughput" rather than "blocked" to support PLG flows
sofia (eng-runtime): agreed. runtime will implement soft quota as priority demotion + token-based throttling rather than hard reject
liam (eng-platform): next steps: liam -> proto policy schema PR, sofia -> telemetry event spec, noah -> console mockups. sync Tuesday 10am
maya (product): thanks. tagging @sofia @liam @noah for follow-ups :thumbsup:
